title: Network Reliability and Redundancy
summary: Analyze alternate paths, single points of failure, and maintenance evidence.
objectives: Identify a single point of failure in a synthetic topology.
Explain failover as an alternate path or system taking over.
Connect reliability to monitoring, documentation, and maintenance.

vocab.def: One component whose failure can interrupt a required service or path.
A change to an alternate available system or path after a failure.
An additional path or component intended to support continuity if another fails.

sections.heading: More than one path
sections.body: Two links are not automatically redundant if they share the same switch, power, or physical route. Trace dependencies before calling a design resilient.

sections.heading: Reliability is operational
sections.body: Monitoring, accurate labels, maintenance planning, and change records help teams know whether an alternate path is available and safe to use.

practice.prompt: Two servers have separate cables but both cables connect to one switch. What dependency remains?
practice.answer: The shared switch remains a single point of failure for both servers.

quiz.question: What makes an alternate path useful during a failure?
options: It is available, documented, and does not depend on the same failed point
It is hidden from the operations team
It is always faster than the primary path
quiz.answer: It is available, documented, and does not depend on the same failed point

lab.objective: Identify dependencies and alternate paths in a synthetic topology.
